title: Normalized kernel of a surjective simplicial quasi-isomorphism is acyclic
statement: Let $X,Y:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be simplicial abelian groups and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For any simplicial abelian group $A$, put $s(A)^{-m}=A_m$ for $m\geq0$, with differential $\sum_{i=0}^m(-1)^id_i$ for $m>0$, zero differential out of degree zero, and zero positive cochain terms. Suppose every $f_m$ is surjective and $s(f)$ induces an isomorphism on every cohomology group [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K_m=\ker(f_m)$, with simplicial operators restricted from $X$. Then $H^r(s(K))=0$ for every integer $r$. Moreover, let $N(K)_0=K_0$ and $N(K)_m=\bigcap_{i=1}^m\ker(d_i:K_m\to K_{m-1})$ for $m>0$, with differential $\partial_m=d_0$ for $m>0$ and $\partial_0:K_0\to0$. Then $\ker\partial_m=\operatorname{im}\partial_{m+1}$ for every $m\geq0$, including $m=0$.

Positive-face normalization as in the existing lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence. Returned proof Steps 1-2.

proof.text: Naturality of $f$ gives $f_j X(\alpha)(k)=Y(\alpha)f_m(k)=0$ for each simplicial operator $X(\alpha):X_m\to X_j$ and $k\in K_m$. Thus all simplicial operators restrict to $K$, and their identities restrict as well. The inclusions $K_m\hookrightarrow X_m$ commute with the alternating face differentials. By degreewise surjectivity, $0\to s(K)\to s(X)\xrightarrow{s(f)}s(Y)\to0$ is short exact in every nonpositive degree; in positive degrees it is the zero sequence. At degree zero the outgoing differential is zero as prescribed.

source.place: Tag 08P1 (lemma-qis-simplicial-abelian-groups), second proof paragraph: replacing X by Ker(f)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to the short exact sequence of integer cochain complexes from Step 1, in the abelian category $\mathrm{Ab}$. For every $r\in\mathbf Z$ it gives the exact segment $H^{r-1}(s(X))\xrightarrow{H^{r-1}(s(f))}H^{r-1}(s(Y))\xrightarrow{\delta}H^r(s(K))\xrightarrow{a}H^r(s(X))\xrightarrow{H^r(s(f))}H^r(s(Y))$. The first map is surjective, so $\delta=0$ and $\ker a=0$. The last map is injective, so $\operatorname{im}a=0$. Hence $H^r(s(K))=0$. These are exactly the cohomology isomorphisms assumed in the item; no boundedness hypothesis is needed, and the argument includes $r=0$ and positive $r$.

source.place: Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain), applied as in Simplicial Tag 08P1, second proof paragraph

proof.text: Write $C_m=K_m$ for the nonnegative alternating chain complex, so $C_m=s(K)^{-m}$ with the same differential. By [lem-cbc-normalized-alternating-homotopy-equivalence], the inclusion $j:N(K)\to C$ has a chain-map homotopy inverse $p$ and maps $h_m:N(K)_m\to N(K)_{m+1}$ with $1-pj=\partial h+h\partial$ (negate the homotopy if necessary). For $m\ge0$ and $z\in\ker\partial_m$, the element $jz$ is a cycle of $C$. Step 2 and the definition $H^{-m}(s(K))=\ker d/\operatorname{im}d$ give $t\in C_{m+1}$ with $dt=jz$. Therefore $\partial(pt+h_mz)=pdt+(1-pj)z=z$. Thus every normalized cycle is a normalized boundary. Conversely every boundary is a cycle because $N(K)$ is a chain complex by the cited statement. For $m=0$, the same computation uses $\partial_0=0$, so it proves surjectivity $\partial_1:N(K)_1\to K_0$ without requiring a nonexistent face out of $K_0$.
